newsitem.title: USA: U.S., North Korea agree on joint MIA searches.
newsitem.headline: U.S., North Korea agree on joint MIA searches.

text.p: The United States and North Korea have agreed to conduct three new joint searches for remains of U.S. troops missing in the North since the Korean War and to review archives in Pyongyang for information on missing Americans, the Pentagon said on Thursday.

But there was no immediate agreement from the North on a request by the United States to interview several U.S. military defectors believed to be living in North Korea since the 1960s, the Defence Department said.

The announcement of the agreement, which was sealed on Wednesday, followed five days of talks between U.S. and North Korean officials in New York last week. Those talks ended on Friday night in what then appeared to be failure.

Larry Greer, a spokesman for the Pentagon office in charge of missing American troops, said he expected the first of the three joint searches to begin within a month and that Washington had agreed to pay Pyongyang $105,500 in expenses for each of the searches.
Greer did not say where the excavations would be held, but said the United States wanted to search sites including single aircraft crashes and perhaps mass burial sites of U.S. troops.

There are more than 8,100 U.S. troops missing in North Korea from the 1950-53 war. Washington also wants to find out the fate of six American troops who defected to the North in the 1960s, four of whom are believed to be still alive in the North.
